title: How A Party Can Improve Classroom Management gement/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Playing on the word 'party,' Linsin proposes a weekly clean-the-room session as a tool for building cooperation, work habits, respect, and maturity in a class. He warns that without careful setup it can devolve into complaints and halfhearted effort, so he offers guidelines: model each cleaning job explicitly, make the activity social and fun with music and teamwork, ensure the jobs require real effort, focus specifically on cleaning tasks like scrubbing, sweeping, and organizing, participate alongside students (ideally pairing with a difficult student), inspect finished work before releasing students to other activities, and treat participation as a privilege withheld from students who refuse to engage. He closes by arguing that physical, cooperative work teaches lessons about capability and self-worth that talking alone cannot, and that the resulting confidence and work habits carry over into everything else students do.
points: A weekly, structured clean-the-room session builds cooperation and work habits better than verbal instruction alone.
Model every cleaning job explicitly before turning students loose, and make the work genuinely effortful, not token.
Add music and teamwork to make the party social and fun rather than a chore.
Pair yourself with your most difficult student during the party to build trust and rapport through shared work.
Treat participation as a privilege—withhold it from students who won't engage, making inclusion something to want.
quotes: It’s a clean-the-room party . And the way it works is simple: one day a week you will supervise a thorough cleaning of your classroom.
Whenever you introduce something new, it’s important to model what you want . To that end, show your students exactly how to perform each job successfully.
Put music on. Let your students work in teams. Let them talk and laugh and have a good time together .
It’s also a good time to pair up with your most difficult student. Working together is a great way to build trust and rapport.
There is something about doing physical work that clicks with students. A weekly cleaning party can impart the virtues of cooperation and hard work better than anything we can say to them.
